In failed state; must be closed before next operation

    posts = db.query(Post).filter(Post.user_id == user_id).all()

What database problem occurs if a User has 1000 posts?
options: Two separate queries execute; N+1 not present
Loads all 1000 posts unnecessarily per request
Memory limit exceeded in ORM
SQLAlchemy raises QueryError

from sqlalchemy.orm import Session, relationship
from sqlalchemy import Column, Integer, String, ForeignKey

class User(Base):
    __tablename__ = "users"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    posts = relationship("Post", back_populates="author")

class Post(Base):
    __tablename__ = "posts"
    id = Column(Integer, primary_key=True)
    user_id = Column(Integer, ForeignKey("users.id"))
    author = relationship("User", back_populates="posts")

def get_user(db: Session, user_id: int):
    user = db.query(User).filter(User.id == user_id).first()
    print(len(user.posts))  # Accessed after query
    return user

What happens when accessing user.posts after the session closes?
options: Posts are pre-loaded and available
DetachedInstanceError raised; posts not accessible
Lazy-loads posts with implicit query
Empty list returned
explanation: Relationship attributes are lazy by default; accessing them outside the session scope raises DetachedInstanceError; use eager loading or access before session closes.

options: Insert statement: 1 query; loop: N queries
Both execute same number of queries
Insert statement: slower due to batch overhead
Loop: faster because results are returned immediately
explanation: insert().values() sends one batch query to the database; the loop sends N individual INSERT queries, making bulk insert dramatically faster.

from sqlalchemy.orm import Session

def update_user(db: Session, user_id: int, new_name: str):
    db.query(User).filter(User.id == user_id).update({User.name: new_name})
    db.commit()
    user = db.query(User).filter(User.id == user_id).first()
    return user

Why does the returned user sometimes show stale data immediately after update?
options: Caching layer delays visibility
Session expiry timeout not configured
SQLAlchemy identity map keeps stale object in memory
Commit error silently ignored
explanation: The query() returns the old User object from session identity cache; call db.expunge_all() before re-querying or use db.refresh(user).

options: Transaction rolls back; data not inserted
Data already committed; exception doesn't roll back
Listener exception retried automatically
Both data and exception logged to database
explanation: after_commit listeners fire after commit succeeds; exceptions in listeners don't roll back the committed transaction.
